name: Türkiye

findings.summary: Turkcell's CEO said the operator had no plans to replace Huawei, its long-time partner; Turkcell's 4G network leaned heavily on Huawei and it had verified a Huawei 5G base station on its commercial network.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 5 reflects Huawei's role in Turkcell's operational 4G RAN as described by Light Reading; Huawei's share of the RAN and any core role were not stated. Single opened source, so uncorroborated. Pre-2020 and not re-confirmed as current; Turkiye Today (Aug 2025, opened) says much of Turkish telecom infrastructure of the past decade relies on Huawei, which suggests continuity but is not operator-specific.

findings.summary: At MWC 2026 Turkcell and Huawei signed three MoUs covering 5G-Advanced and standalone 5G expansion, 6G and autonomous-network research, and AI infrastructure, cloud platforms and model training in Türkiye. No value disclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Source is labelled as Huawei-sponsored content, so treated as S4 corporate marketing: evidence the MoUs were announced, not of deployment. Tier 1 (non-binding MoUs). A DCD product-news item on an earlier Turkcell-Huawei strategic cooperation agreement appeared in search but was not opened.

findings.summary: China Development Bank lent Turkcell US$250m in two collateral-free tranches (five- and seven-year), to be spent in 2012-2013 on Huawei products and services, per a disclosure to the Istanbul Stock Exchange.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 4: financing closed (exchange disclosure reported). Pole prc because the financed equipment is Huawei's; China Development Bank recorded as financier. Pre-2020 and not re-checked as current; loans would have matured by about 2019. The underlying KAP/ISE filing was not opened.

findings.summary: At MWC 2026 Turkcell selected Ericsson to co-develop, integrate and deploy advanced RAN toward 5G-Advanced, and signed MoUs on cloud RAN/automation and 6G research; it also signed a Mavenir MoU on AI services in its IMS core.
findings.analyst_inference: Ericsson is Swedish, so pole third. Coded tier 2 because the source does not say the RAN selection is a signed contract or give a value; if it is a binding award this is tier 3. Mavenir (US) MoU is tier 1 and folded in here rather than coded separately. Whether Ericsson and Huawei split Turkcell's 5G RAN is unknown.

findings.summary: Turkcell and Google Cloud announced Türkiye's first hyperscale data centre, to host a Google Cloud region: about US$3bn in total, Google US$2bn over ten years and Turkcell about US$1bn to 2032, with clusters planned for 2028-2029.

sources.publisher: Investment Office of the Presidency of Türkiye

findings.analyst_inference: Pole domestic because AGBI describes Turkcell as the infrastructure provider (owner-operator); Google's cloud region inside it is a us cloud-layer fact covered by the global layers. Ownership split is not stated explicitly, so if Google co-owns the building the pole could be us. Tier 1: announcement only, no construction start found. Site and MW capacity not disclosed.

findings.summary: TÜBİTAK ULAKBİM added 192 Nvidia H200 GPUs to its ARF-ACC system in 2025 (it began with H100s in 2024); the system ranked 145th on the November 2025 TOP500 and serves research, public and private AI workloads.
findings.analyst_inference: Equipment rule: accelerator vendor Nvidia, so pole us; operator is the state research council. Total GPU count and integrator not stated. Operational as of November 2025; not re-confirmed for October 2026, so still_current left null.

findings.controller: TÜBİTAK; HAVELSAN; T3 Foundation with Baykar
findings.local_actor: Government of Türkiye (AI Vision and Action Plan 2026-2030)
findings.summary: Türkiye's 2026-2030 AI action plan reaffirmed a Turkish large language model effort, citing TÜBİTAK, the T3 Foundation with Baykar, and HAVELSAN's 9-billion-parameter model, and made the public sector primary customer for domestic AI.

sources.publisher: Investment Office of the Presidency of Türkiye

findings.analyst_inference: Pole domestic on the assumption that weights are held by Turkish state-linked bodies; whether the models are trained from scratch or fine-tuned from foreign open weights is not stated, so base_model and base_model_pole are null. Tier 1: policy commitment. Anadolu is state-affiliated (S4) and its page could not be fetched. Separately, New Mind AI (Turkish firm) holds a June 2025 EuroHPC MareNostrum5 allocation for a Turkish LLM (opened, not coded).

applications.null_reason: one search on Hikvision/Dahua safe-city or police use in Türkiye returned only vendor marketing, market reports and non-Turkish projects; no Turkish procurement found

power.null_reason: no AI/data-centre-specific power evidence surfaced; budget spent on other layers

research_gaps: Which vendors supply Turkcell, Türk Telekom and Vodafone Türkiye 5G RAN and core after the October 2025 auction and April 2026 launch? Huawei vs Ericsson/Nokia split per operator.
What domestic-equipment (e.g. ULAK) share do the 5G licence conditions require, and has any operator deployed ULAK 5G base stations?
Is Ericsson's March 2026 Turkcell RAN selection a binding contract (value, scope)?
Ownership structure and site of the Turkcell-Google hyperscale data centre; construction start.
Huawei Cloud Istanbul region and Alibaba Cloud's announced Turkey region (global layer): any government or Turkcell tenancy?
Base model and weights control of HAVELSAN's 9B model and the TÜBİTAK / T3-Baykar Turkish LLMs.
Odine-Supermicro AI infrastructure partnership (June 2026, TelecomTV): any concrete GPU deployment and chip vendor.
Chinese-made CCTV (Hikvision/Dahua) in Turkish municipal or police systems; any Huawei safe-city contract.
Did US pressure (Pompeo-era warnings) produce any formal Huawei restriction in Turkish networks?
